deskyard forward: map TCP ports between this machine and the desktop

Usage: deskyard [-d NAME] forward [-R] PORT[:PORT]...

Maps TCP ports both ways until Ctrl-C, over the remote access API (no port is
opened anywhere else). Each argument is one mapping. PORT or LOCAL:DESKTOP:
this machine's 127.0.0.1:LOCAL becomes localhost:DESKTOP in the desktop (a dev
server here, reachable by the desktop's browser). -R PORT or -R DESKTOP:LOCAL
(reverse; one -R before each such mapping): the desktop's localhost:DESKTOP
becomes 127.0.0.1:LOCAL here. Both ends listen on loopback only; the desktop
won't listen below 1024 (plain forward only; -R just dials, so -R 80:8080
works). A port in use on either side fails that mapping, which is retried, and
the others carry on. When the connection drops (the desktop stops or restarts,
the network blips) it keeps its local listeners, closes open connections and
reconnects with backoff (1 s up to 30 s). It exits only on Ctrl-C, or when the
token is refused. Run it in the background. Inside a desktop it needs -d too.

Arguments:
  PORT       string...   required  a mapping: PORT or LOCAL:DESKTOP; after -R, PORT or DESKTOP:LOCAL

Options:
  -R, --reverse        the next mapping is reverse: a port in the desktop
                       becomes a port here

Prints: one line per mapping each time it goes live: "in LOCAL DESKTOP" or
  "out DESKTOP 127.0.0.1:LOCAL"; on stderr one line per state change
  (linked, lost and retrying, port in use)

Examples:
  deskyard -d alice forward 3000 -R 5173
  deskyard -d alice forward 8080:3000 &
  deskyard -d alice forward -R 9229:19229

Where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop too, since it maps ports between two machines. Ports are LOCAL:DESKTOP, or DESKTOP:LOCAL after -R. The desktop won't listen below 1024. "Linked to ..." and the out lines appear when the link is accepted, before the desktop side is known to run
Exit codes: 0 after Ctrl-C, 1 when the token is refused (401) or no remote is set up, 2 usage error
